topic_and_scope: A MaxEnt-based assessment of Papilio xuthus geographic distribution under current and future climates, identifying environmental drivers, migration tendencies, and conservation implications for East Asia.
main_themes: Climate-driven distribution shifts and centroid migration of Papilio xuthus in East Asia
Modeling approaches and key environmental drivers shaping butterfly distribution
Conservation planning and policy implications under multiple future climate scenarios
main_findings: Papilio xuthus has a wide current distribution in East Asia, with high-suitability areas concentrated in China, Japan, North Korea, and South Korea, particularly along the Yangtze River basin.

Under IPCC SSP scenarios, high-suitability areas generally decrease and shift northeast, with China showing the most pronounced reductions; centroid analysis indicates a consistent northeastward migration in future decades.

key_gaps.description: Explicit limitation: the study relies on a correlative MaxEnt model and acknowledges potential overprediction of suitable habitat without independent field validation or incorporation of biotic interactions (e.g., host-plant distributions) or dispersal constraints.

Implicit need: integration of host-plant (Rutaceae) distributions and other biotic factors, as well as species interactions and dispersal/migration processes, to refine predictions and improve ecological realism.

future_directions.title: Field-based validation of predicted high-suitability zones
future_directions.rationale: To ensure ecological realism of SDM outputs, implement targeted occupancy surveys and presence-absence checks in current and predicted future high-suitability areas (e.g., Yangtze basin per China and northeast regions). This should include standardized detection probability estimates and periodic re-surveys to refine model parameters and update predictions with new occurrence data over 2–3 years, incorporating citizen science where feasible.

future_directions.title: Couple Papilio xuthus distribution with host-plant (Rutaceae) availability
future_directions.rationale: Larval oligophagy on Rutaceae ties butterfly distribution to host-plant presence. Develop joint or stacked SDMs that incorporate Rutaceae distributions and their climate suitability, plus host-plant phenology, to generate more ecologically realistic forecasts and identify areas where host plants may limit butterfly range expansion under climate change.

future_directions.title: Incorporate dispersal, connectivity, and landscape barriers
future_directions.rationale: Predicted range shifts assume potential colonization; real-world movement is constrained by mountains, urbanization, and habitat fragmentation. Use connectivity/least-cost path or circuit theory approaches to identify viable migration corridors from current to future suitable habitats and propose habitat restoration or corridor creation where needed.

future_directions.title: Adopt ensemble and multi-model SDMs to quantify uncertainty
future_directions.rationale: Relying on a single modeling framework limits robustness. Run multiple SDMs (e.g., MaxEnt, GBM, RF, GLM) and combine with ensemble forecasting to quantify uncertainty, produce consensus maps, and provide probabilistic guidance for conservation planning under varying climate projections.

future_directions.title: Develop mechanistic, physiological models of thermal tolerance
future_directions.rationale: Correlative models may mispredict under novel climates. Gather species-specific physiological data (thermal tolerance, development rates, survivorship across temperatures) and build mechanistic models (e.g., degree-day or energy budget models) to cross-validate and refine SDM predictions, especially under warming scenarios.

future_directions.title: Assess impacts of climate extremes and variability
future_directions.rationale: Beyond mean climate changes, extreme precipitation and drought events can dramatically affect both P. xuthus and host-plant health. Integrate extreme-weather indices into scenario analyses (e.g., drought/flood frequency and intensity) to identify hotspots of vulnerability and to guide risk-informed conservation actions.

future_directions.title: Translate predictions into concrete conservation actions and policy support
future_directions.rationale: Use model outputs to designate priority protected areas and restoration targets for host plants, plan connectivity corridors, and inform urban biodiversity initiatives. Develop actionable guidelines for land-use planning, habitat restoration, and adaptive management, with monitoring frameworks and collaboration among researchers, policymakers, and local communities.
